runner.runtime: PHP 7.0.30 from the existing vulnerable/web-dvwa image
compatibility_rewrites: Removed PHP 7.1 nullable type declarations and class constant visibility at load time.
Converted array destructuring to list() syntax at load time.
Provided str_starts_with and mb_substr compatibility functions.
runner.reason: The host has no PHP CLI and pulling a PHP 8 image failed while fetching the Docker Hub authorization token.
runner.assessment: The rewrites preserve scan rule and request semantics, but this is not an unmodified production QingScan deployment.

method: Run the complete upstream directory dictionary, technology fingerprint and WAF fingerprint checks.
Run VulnScan on the root and crawled URLs.
Run SqlInjectScan only on crawled URLs that contain a query string.
Report directory hits separately from confirmed vulnerability findings.

dvwa.raw_vuln_duplicate_reason: The same robots.txt rule was emitted once for each VulnScan input URL.

comparison_notes: A successful directory request proves that a path exists; it does not by itself prove a vulnerability.
QingScan found useful candidates such as Juice Shop /metrics and /api-docs, but its own vulnerability phase did not classify them.
The crawler did not execute the Juice Shop single-page application, so it discovered no API URLs or query parameters for injection checks.
The upstream client was not instrumented for a complete request count; DirScan alone sends one baseline request plus 329 candidate requests per target.
limits: Unauthenticated root scan only; no DVWA login or challenge-specific seed URLs.
No labelled full challenge set, so vulnerability recall and false-positive percentages are not reported.
